Behind almost every cup of coffee, there’s a woman carrying the weight of labor, caregiving, and trauma — often in silence. In Colombia, women coffee farmers face some of the highest mental health risks, yet almost no access to tailored care.

SANA exists to change that. We provide women coffee farmers with tailored, integrative mental health support so they can heal, grow, and reclaim their dignity.

💙You can make this possible. For just $25 a month, you give one woman access to our program — therapy, tools, and the chance to live a healthier, more fulfilling life.

👉 Donate today. Help us break the silence and bring hope to the women who are the backbone of coffee.
 🔗 Go to sanaprograms.org/donate or find link in our bio.

We’re calling on coffee roasters and cafés to join us (@sana_programs) in supporting the mental health and wellbeing of women coffee farmers through our October Give-Back Campaign.

Our program is designed to help these women live healthier & more fulfilling lives while supporting them in gaining the emotional tools and agency to thrive within their families and communities.

Why October?
 October kicks off with International Coffee Day a perfect moment to reflect on the people behind every cup. It’s also a powerful month for mental health advocacy with Mental Illness Awareness Week (October 5–11) and World Mental Health Day (October 10) making this the perfect time to take meaningful action at origin.

How Your Café or Roastery Can Join:

* Pick a drink → donate 20% of its sales throughout October to SANA.
* Pick a coffee offering → donate 10% per bag sold to SANA throughout October.

Let’s make October a month of real impact where mental health becomes the foundation of gender equity and sustainability in the coffee industry.

☕ Ready to join?
Comment below or email us at info@sanaprograms.org so we can send you the participation guidelines.

We’ve measured the yield, we’ve invested in quality, and more resistant varieties, but if we imagine a future where coffee is available we intrinsically have to start prioritizing the well-being of the humans producing it. Because if these humans are struggling mentally, emotionally, and physically, it doesn't matter how much coffee they produce, or how much they get paid for that coffee, they won't have the energy, the mental bandwidth, and emotional tools to thrive as coffee farmers.

💙💐🌺🌸🌼🌻🌷We care for our gardens with love. Are we doing the same for ourselves?
At SANA, we asked our participants to share something meaningful with us — the gardens they tend to each day. With patience, they water, prune, and nourish each plant with care. Their gardens flourish because they show up for them, over and over again.
But then came a beautiful and honest reflection:
“We often forget to be as kind, loving, and caring to ourselves as we are to our gardens. But today, we promise to ask this question often and to prioritize our self-care time.”

This is the heart of SANA: a space where women begin to reconnect with themselves. Where they treat their inner world with the same tenderness they give to the soil.

💙 Today, we invite you to do the same and to help us grow this work.

Although the brain makes up only 2% of the body weight, it uses 20% of our daily energy. Every thought, emotion, and decision depends on it.

At SANA, we know that the brain, body, and mental health are deeply connected. When one is out of balance, the others feel it too. That’s why we support women coffee farmers in Colombia with integrative mental health care and wellness programs that nurture the mind and nervous system, helping them process stress, build resilience, and feel supported.

This is our first post — Wow! 🎉 💙
We are so excited to begin sharing our story with you finally. We’ll be launching in seven days, and you’ll have the opportunity to be part of this movement by supporting us with your donations to help bring mental health care and wellness to more women coffee farmers. 

From storytelling to action: 
When our founder, @luciabawot, published We Belong— a book showcasing the lives of Colombian women coffee farmers — she couldn’t ignore the emotional weight of their stories. 

What started as a photography project evolved into a mission. After hearing women say, “I’ve never told anyone this before,” Lucia recognized that mental health care isn’t just a need; it’s a right. 

This realization led to Beans to Minds, a small yet impactful mental health pilot that served 39 women coffee farmers and pickers in Colombia. Today, that pilot has evolved into SANA — an 5-month integrative mental health care & wellness program for women coffee farmers that aims to: reduce stigma surrounding mental health, break cycles of silence, strengthen emotional awareness, and foster personal agency, combining teletherapy, virtual education, and community-based support. 

Follow along as we continue this journey and share the details of what we do and who we do it for.
